audit.method: Read from the full term sheet by one AI reviewer, then checked against it twice by independent AI reviewers: first every line of the record against the document, then the document section by section against the record. Not signed off by a person. Every quote is looked up in the PDF text each time the tool runs.
audit.open_points:
Final record: C:\Users\AFarid\Documents\Hackathon\key_credit_terms\data\audited\aon_2026.json (checker: structure OK, 85 quotes exact, none loose, missing or on another page). All 11 pages were read in the dump and on the page images. Every amount, ratio, period, date and party in the record matches the term sheet, and nothing in the term sheet that belongs in a template row is missing. Pricing (page 11 grid), Required Lenders, yield protection and indemnity have no template row and are not recorded.

Resolved from the document:
- Closed lists (doubt 5): the Documentation Principles themselves say the agreement 'shall contain only the representations, warranties, covenants and events of default set forth below' (page 6), so the six 'None' rows stand.
- Security / ranking (doubt 3): stated as derived points; this is the style guide's own worked example.
- Step levels (doubt 9): 4.50x, 4.25x, 4.00x and 3.75x confirmed on the page 7 image; they cannot all be quoted within three quotes.
- Not_stated rows re-tested by search: no Barclays, commitment amounts, coverage test, post-closing obligation, budget, or jurisdiction of Aon plc anywhere in the term sheet.

The term sheet itself cannot settle these:
1. Facility: the $1.0bn sub-limit is for 'the UK Borrower' (singular) while three UK Borrowers are defined; aggregate or per-borrower is not stated. The line flags it.
2. Accordion: $1.8bn as the cap on the increase is the only reading consistent with a $3.0bn Facility Amount, but the term sheet does not say so. The line now says it is a reading.
3. Interest cover start date: it runs from the 'Closing Date', defined only in the separate Term Loan Facility Term Sheet, so the date cannot be fixed from this document. The leverage proviso also refers to 'any Term Lender' and a 'Consolidated Leverage Ratio', wording that appears carried over from the term loan.
4. Permitted guarantees: 'None' under the closed-list rule; whether the indebtedness covenant catches guarantees is only in the Existing Revolving Credit Agreements.
5. Transferability: the Borrower consent standard is only in the Existing Revolving Credit Agreements; the line keeps the required prefix as 'Borrower consent: not stated in term sheet'.
6. Mandatory prepayment: the term sheet is silent rather than saying there are none; the row is stated only because change of control is addressed, as an event of default with no ownership trigger.
7. Condition precedent (f) refers to 'Existing Credit Agreements', an undefined term, read as the Existing Revolving Credit Agreements.
8. The whole term sheet is 'not final and subject to change'.

Format points left as they are: 11 lines run 244-333 characters (guide about 250, hard limit 420), the longest being the cash-netting line in Other Select Definitions, which uses a 'Net debt / cash netting:' prefix that is not one of the four template prefixes.

doc.title: Aon North America, Inc., Aon Corporation, Aon Global Holdings plc, Aon Global Limited and Aon UK Limited - Summary of the Revolving Facility
doc.notes: Stand-alone term sheet (marked 'Posting Version', undated) summarising a new $3.0bn five-year revolving facility for the Aon group, which replaces the two Existing Revolving Credit Agreements (2021 and 2023) and sits alongside a separate $4.0bn term loan facility (own term sheet) for the acquisition of USI Advantage Corp. The terms are on pages 1-10 in a label / value layout; page 11 is the ratings-based pricing grid (Schedule I). It is a new facility, not an amendment, so there are no existing / proposed columns. Representations, the non-financial covenants and events of default are given as lists with little detail and are to be 'substantially similar to' the Existing Revolving Credit Agreements as in effect on August 30, 2026; definitions, assignments, yield protection and indemnity defer to those agreements, and the terms are stated to be not final and subject to change.
